title: Monic prime factorization over a normal domain
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and let $F\in A[T]$ be monic [def-weil-polynomial-ring], meaning its leading coefficient is $1$. There exist $s\geq0$ and monic polynomials $h_1,\ldots,h_s\in A[T]$ of positive degree such that $F=\prod_{j=1}^s h_j$, every image $(h_j)_K\in K[T]$ is irreducible, and every quotient $A[T]/(h_j)$ is a nonzero integral domain [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Irreducible means nonzero, nonunit, with a unit factor in every factorization in $K[T]$. Repeated factors are allowed, and the empty product is $1$. Moreover, if $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and every coefficient of $F$ below its leading coefficient belongs to $\mathfrak m$, the factors can be chosen with every coefficient of every $h_j$ below its leading coefficient in $\mathfrak m$. No Noetherian, factorial, completeness, or separability hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

source.place: Tag 00H6, lemma-polynomials-divide, clauses (1) and (2), lines 8432-8479: integral coefficients of monic factors, and lower coefficients in the radical of the lower-coefficient ideal. Combined with field-polynomial factorization as in EGA IV4 proof of Theorem 21.14.1, final paragraph (online translation; EGA IV4 WANTED locally).

proof.text: If $F=1$, take $s=0$; all assertions are vacuous. Otherwise $F_K$ is a nonzero nonunit in $K[T]$: a nonzero constant is a unit over a field, and a monic constant is $1$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-polynomial-irreducible-factorization] to $F_K$. Write $F_K=u\prod_j p_j$, where $u\in K^\times$ and each $p_j$ is irreducible; each $p_j$ has positive degree, since a constant is either $0$ or a unit over a field. Put $c_j=\operatorname{lc}(p_j)\ne0$ and $g_j=c_j^{-1}p_j$. Multiplication by the unit constant $c_j^{-1}$ preserves irreducibility by its definition. Comparing the highest coefficients gives $u\prod_jc_j=1$, so $F_K=\prod_jg_j$ with all $g_j$ monic, irreducible and of positive degree. This is a finite list with multiplicities, not a list of distinct factors.

source.place: Tag 0BC1 (lemma-polynomial-ring-UFD), one variable over a field; normalization by leading coefficients written out by Q72

proof.text: Each $g_j$ divides $F_K$. Apply [lem-sfb-normal-monic-divisor-descent] to $A$, its fraction field $K$, the monic $F$ and this monic divisor, obtaining $h_j\in A[T]$ with $(h_j)_K=g_j$. The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow K$ is injective, so the highest nonzero coefficient and degree are preserved: each $h_j$ is monic and has the same positive degree as $g_j$. The coefficientwise image of $F-\prod_jh_j$ is zero; injectivity on each coefficient gives $F=\prod_jh_j$ in $A[T]$. This uses normality only for the descent, not a factorial assumption on $A$.

Fix $j$ and put $d=\deg h_j>0$. The coefficient inclusion induces a unital ring map $\iota:A[T]/(h_j)\to K[T]/(g_j)$, sending the class of $P$ to the class of $P_K$; it is well defined since $(h_j)_K=g_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], over $A$ and over $K$ these quotients have bases $1,t,\ldots,t^{d-1}$. If $b=\sum_{i<d}a_it^i$ maps to zero, linear independence of the $K$-basis gives $a_i=0$ in $K$ for every $i$, hence $a_i=0$ in $A$. Thus $\iota$ is injective. By [lem-trf-irreducible-polynomial-quotient-field], irreducibility of $g_j$ makes $K[T]/(g_j)$ a field; a field is nonzero and has no zero divisors, since $xy=0$ with $x\ne0$ gives $y=x^{-1}xy=0$. The source of $\iota$ is nonzero because $\iota(1)=1\ne0$, and if $bc=0$ its image has a zero factor, whence injectivity gives $b=0$ or $c=0$. This proves the required domain assertion without treating irreducibility in $A[T]$ as primality.

source.place: Tag 09FI (example-quotient-polymial-ring), quotient by an irreducible polynomial is a field; injectivity written by Q72 using the cited monic power bases

proof.text: For the local assertion use the same factors, and reduce $F=h_jq_j$, where $q_j=\prod_{i\ne j}h_i$, modulo $\mathfrak m$. The ring $k=A/\mathfrak m$ is a field: for $a\notin\mathfrak m$, maximality gives $1=ra+x$ with $x\in\mathfrak m$, so the class of $r$ is its inverse. Both reduced factors remain monic. If their degrees are $d,e$, the top product coefficient is $1$ and $d+e=n=\deg F$. Let $r,t$ be their lowest nonzero exponents. In the convolution at exponent $r+t$ the sole nonzero term is the product of these two nonzero coefficients, so their product has lowest exponent $r+t$. But the reduced product is $T^n$, hence $r+t=n=d+e$. Since $r\le d$ and $t\le e$, one has $r=d$ and $t=e$. Thus $\overline h_j=T^d$, which says exactly that every lower coefficient of $h_j$ lies in $\mathfrak m$. The empty product and constant complementary factor cause no exception.
